title: `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` references undeclared `session`; runtime ReferenceError blocks completion
evidence: Inside `handleCardRating` (line 184) the success branch (line 216) calls `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` on lines 230-234. The `useSession()` import on line 68 is destructured as `const { user } = useSession();` on line 137 — `session` is **never** declared in this component's scope. The `useSession()` return type in `apps/primary-advantage/node_modules/@reading-advantage/auth-client/dist/index.d.ts:47-51` is `{ user: AuthUser | null; isAuthenticated: boolean; isLoading: boolean }` (no `session` field). The optional-chained `session?.user` is a JavaScript ReferenceError, not a TypeScript no-op — `session` is undeclared, so any attempt to read it throws `ReferenceError: session is not defined`. This same anti-pattern is duplicated across 7 sibling files in `apps/primary-advantage/components/lesson/games/`: `lesson-vocabulary-flashcard-card.tsx:238`, `lesson-sentence-order.tsx:306`, `lesson-sentence-order-word.tsx:288`, `lesson-sentence-matching.tsx:219`, `lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx:217`, `lesson-sentence-cloze-test.tsx:526`. This is a fork-specific pattern: the prior Reading Advantage implementation likely used an `useSession()` that returned `{ session, ... }` (the auth-client provider code at `node_modules/@reading-advantage/auth-client/dist/index.js:36-37` previously read `data.session?.user` from a fetch response). The fork's lesson-games components were never updated to the slimmed-down `useSession` shape.
impact: Critical. The success path of the final card's rating handler is unreachable in a working state — the ReferenceError thrown by `update({...})` aborts the surrounding `startTransition` callback, so `setGameState(GameState.COMPLETED)` on line 244 still runs (it's outside the transition), but the XP/activity logging already completed on lines 218-229 will have its effect obscured by the JS exception, and the user sees the completion screen with the wrong XP if any. More importantly, the prior context (line 202 `setPaused(true)`, line 217 `setSessionComplete(true)`) is left in a half-applied state because the exception propagates through the transition.
recommendation: Replace `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` with either (a) `update({ user })` — the `useSession()` return value is the correct source and the action surface should accept it, or (b) delete the call entirely and rely on the `updateUserActivity` server action (line 218) for the authoritative state update. The auth-client package should be expanded to expose an `update()` action (or the call removed) so the surrounding 7 files can be patched in one mechanical change. Track this under a new `primary_advantage_session_update_bug_<date>` Measure track for a sweep across all 7 files.

title: Dead `safeCompletionData` object: built on lines 260-266 but never read in completion JSX
evidence: When `shouldShowCompletion` is true (line 258), the code constructs a `safeCompletionData` fallback (lines 260-266) with `xpEarned: 20`, `timeTaken: 0`, default `sessionStats`, and `completionDate`. However, the completion JSX on lines 268-330 never references `safeCompletionData`. Instead, the rendered values are: `UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_FLASHCARDS` literal (line 300), `formatTime(timer)` from the QuizContext (line 308), and `completedCards}/{words.length}` (line 316). The `completionData` state (declared on line 120) is similarly never assigned anywhere in the file — `setCompletionData` is never called. The `safeCompletionData` is a defensive scaffold with no consumer.
impact: High. The completion screen always shows the static `UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_FLASHCARDS` enum value as the XP, regardless of what XP was actually earned via the rating flow. For a primary-student app, the completion screen is a key motivation loop (badge for finishing the activity). Showing a static value, plus a wall-clock from the QuizContext timer (which keeps running if `setPaused(true)` is racy, see finding 005), creates an inaccurate "you earned X XP" feedback. The user has no real completion record because `setCompletionData` is never invoked from the rating handler either.
recommendation: Either (a) actually wire `setCompletionData({ xpEarned: UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_FLASHCARDS, timeTaken: timer, sessionStats, isExistingCompletion: false, completionDate: new Date().toISOString() })` inside the success branch of the transition (line 217), or (b) refactor the JSX to read the in-scope values directly (line 300 → computed `xpEarned` from the transition result, line 308 → capture `elapsedTime` at completion time, line 316 → derive from the same captured snapshot). Delete the unused `safeCompletionData` literal once a real source is in place.

title: Type-safety violation: `flipped: false` set on `FlashcardWord` object, but `FlashcardWord` interface has no `flipped` field
evidence: The `FlashcardWord` interface (lines 94-102) declares fields: `id`, `sentence`, `translation`, `state`, `startTime?`, `endTime?`, `audioUrl?` — no `flipped` property. However, in `handleCardRating` (line 184) the `setWords` call on lines 193-197 maps over the array and sets `{ ...card, flipped: false }` on the next card. TypeScript with `strict: true` and the AGENTS.md "TypeScript strictness" rule should reject this assignment, but the project may be running with `noImplicitAny: false` or a similar looser setting (verified by the fact that the `as FlashcardWord[]` cast on line 168 already suppresses stricter checks). The downstream code on lines 567-590 then reads `currentCard.state` and never reads `.flipped`, so the property is dead — it is set on every rating but never consulted.
impact: Medium. The `flipped` field is dead state written on every card advance (line 195). It is a leftover from an earlier version of the component where the card itself tracked a `flipped` boolean for the question/answer transition. The current implementation uses the `showAnswer` state on line 114 for that purpose. The dead `flipped` write also forces a re-render of the entire `words` array (since `setWords` is called with a new array reference) on every rating, which is unnecessary because the consumers don't read `flipped`.
recommendation: Remove lines 193-197 entirely — the `setWords` call has no purpose if `flipped` is not read anywhere. If a future feature does need per-card `flipped` state, add it to the `FlashcardWord` interface (line 94-102) first so the type contract is explicit, and audit the codebase for read sites before re-adding the write.

title: Stale closure: `finalCompleted` reads `completedCards` from before the current setState takes effect
evidence: In `handleCardRating`, when the last card is being rated (line 199 else branch), the code reads `const finalCompleted = completedCards + 1;` on line 200. The `completedCards` value here is the React state value captured at the closure where this rating call was created — i.e. it does not include the `+1` from `setCompletedCards((prev) => prev + 1)` on line 191 in a prior iteration. The very next line (201) calls `setCompletedCards(finalCompleted)` with a non-functional setter, which sets state to the stale value + 1, but React batches updates so a subsequent read of `completedCards` will see the value at the time of the next render. The whole pattern of using a non-functional setState to compute the next value from a stale closure is the bug the functional form `setCompletedCards((prev) => prev + 1)` (used on line 191) was designed to prevent.
impact: Medium. On the last card, the displayed `completedCards` after completion is `previousValue + 1`, not `(previousValue + 1)` from the prior `setCompletedCards` callback. If the rating handler is invoked multiple times in rapid succession (e.g. user clicks two rating buttons in quick succession), the second invocation's read of `completedCards` is still the original, leading to `finalCompleted` collisions and the progress bar / completion screen showing off-by-one counts. For a primary-student flashcard activity the bug is silent and rarely noticed.
recommendation: Replace lines 200-201 with `setCompletedCards((prev) => prev + 1);` to use the functional form consistently with line 191. Delete the `const finalCompleted` line — it is not used anywhere else in the function. Better: since `finalCompleted` is not referenced after the assignment, just remove both lines and rely on the final `setCompletedCards((prev) => prev + 1)` inside the transition's success path (move the increment to after the `allSuccess` check so the count reflects reality).

title: `setGameState(GameState.COMPLETED)` runs synchronously before the async transition resolves; UI shows "completed" while the rating save is in-flight
evidence: `handleCardRating`'s final-card branch (line 199 onward) calls `setPaused(true)` on line 202, then `startTransition(async () => { ... })` on lines 203-242. Inside the transition, the rating reviews are dispatched (line 212), checked for success (line 214), and only on success does `updateUserActivity` run (line 218). The very last line of the else branch, line 244, calls `setGameState(GameState.COMPLETED)` **outside and after** the transition. Because `startTransition` is non-blocking — the callback runs async, but line 244 executes immediately on the same microtask — the component re-renders into the `GameState.COMPLETED` branch (line 255) before the transition's `updateUserActivity` call resolves. If the transition throws, the `try/catch` on lines 204/238 swallows it, the `setSessionComplete(true)` on line 217 is never set, and the user is shown the completion celebration screen anyway.
impact: High. A primary-student user who fails the last rating (server returns `success: false`) sees the same celebration UI as a successful pass. The activity log on the server may not record the completion, but the client treats it as completed. This decouples the perceived success from the actual persisted state, which violates the AGENTS.md "Auth/session/role/tenant boundaries" principle (the UI claims an outcome the system did not record).
recommendation: Move `setGameState(GameState.COMPLETED)` from line 244 into the transition's success branch (after `setSessionComplete(true)` on line 217, before the `else { toast.error(...) }` on line 236). On the failure branch, stay in the current state so the user can retry. If the goal is to show the celebration regardless, render a separate "in-flight" UI until the transition resolves.

title: Six dead `useState` hooks: `isSubmitting`, `isDeleting`, `elapsedTime`, `startTime`, `isTimerRunning`, `sessionComplete`
evidence: Six `useState` declarations are present but their setters are never invoked in the component:
impact: Low. Six state slots are allocated, each triggering a no-op React internal subscription. Bundle size and React reconciler work are minor but real. The dead state indicates the component was partially refactored from an earlier skeleton (the comment on line 253 says "for debugging" — a stale debug comment). Future maintainers will assume these are part of the contract and may add writes that never propagate, or reads from `sessionStats` that always return zero.
recommendation: Delete lines 115-119, 123-128, 132, and the `setSessionComplete(true)` call on line 217. Also delete the "for debugging" comment on line 253. If `isSubmitting` was meant to drive the `setIsSubmitting` write during the transition, replace it with `useTransition`'s `isPending` (already available on line 130) and gate the rating buttons on `disabled={isPending}` (already done on lines 634, 645, 656, 667).

title: Ten unused imports from `lucide-react` and `next-intl`; bundle-size and maintenance debt
evidence: The import block on lines 15-42 imports 26 named exports from `lucide-react` (Trophy, Clock, Play, Pause, RotateCcw, Eye, Volume2, ThumbsUp, ThumbsDown, AlertTriangle, Zap, SkipForward, Target, Brain, Lightbulb, GraduationCap, Sparkles, Star, CheckCircle, BookOpen, AlertCircle, RefreshCw, Languages, RefreshCcwIcon, Loader2) and `useLocale` from `next-intl` (line 42). A scope-confined grep of the file shows the following 10 symbols are imported but never used in the component body:
impact: Low. Each unused import adds bytes to the client bundle (lucide-react tree-shakes per-symbol but still has to scan the module graph). More importantly, it is a maintenance signal: the component was scaffolded from a template that included the full icon palette, and the cleanup was missed. Future icon additions follow the same pattern, so the gap will grow.
recommendation: Remove lines 18, 19, 22, 27, 34, 35, 36, 38, 40, and 42. Verify the build (`pnpm --filter primary-advantage build`) still passes after the change. Add a lint rule (`no-unused-vars` from ESLint with TypeScript's `noUnusedLocals: true`) if not already enabled — the AGENTS.md "TypeScript strictness" rule implies this should be on.

title: Hardcoded `"th"` default language for sentence translation; primary-students on `cn`/`tw`/`vi` see a Thai translation on first load
evidence: The state initializer on line 129 is `useState<string>("th")` — Thai is the default regardless of the user's locale. The `SENTENCE_LANGUAGES` map (line 411, imported from `../../flashcards/deck-view`) supports `th`, `cn`, `tw`, `vi`, and `en`. The translation is read on line 620 as `currentCard.translation[selectedLanguage]` — so for a user whose `next-intl` locale is `cn` (Simplified Chinese), the card is loaded and the user must manually switch to Chinese in the start-game picker (lines 433-487) before answering. There is no `useLocale()`-driven default. The `useLocale` import on line 42 is unused (see finding 007), so the intent to drive the default from the active locale was likely abandoned mid-refactor.
impact: Medium. Primary-student adaptation risk. A 7-year-old student on the `cn` or `tw` locale who clicks through the "show answer" reveal (line 685) sees a Thai translation as the answer. They have to scroll up to the language picker (which is on the start screen, not the playing screen) and... actually they can't change it once playing because the picker is only rendered in `GameState.START_GAME` (line 413). They would have to navigate back, switch, and restart. The first-encounter UX is broken for non-Thai locales.
recommendation: Replace line 129 with `useState<string>(useLocale() ?? "th")` (and use the `useLocale` import on line 42 that is currently dead — see finding 007). Add a fallback chain: `useLocale() ?? "en"` if no app locale is set. Verify the `SENTENCE_LANGUAGES` map keys include the `useLocale()` value for all 5 supported locales (`th`, `cn`, `tw`, `vi`, `en`).

title: `if (gameState === GameState.COMPLETED) return;` on line 161 is dead: the preceding line 155 just set state to LOADING
evidence: `loadGameData` is declared on line 153 as `async () => {`. The first executable line inside the `try` block is `setGameState(GameState.LOADING);` (line 155). The next conditional on line 161 is `if (gameState === GameState.COMPLETED) return;`. Because the function just set the state to `LOADING`, the captured `gameState` from the closure (line 161) is the value **before** the `setGameState` call was issued — which is whatever the state was when `loadGameData` was invoked, not the new `LOADING` value (React state updates are async and not visible in the same closure). In normal operation `loadGameData` is only called from: the `useEffect` on line 250 (initial mount, `gameState` is the initial value `LOADING`), the error retry button on line 374 (`gameState` is `ERROR`), and `shouldShowCompletion` does not call `loadGameData`. So the only time the guard could fire is if the function is called while `gameState` is already `COMPLETED` — which never happens in this file because there is no caller that does so. The guard is a leftover from the commented-out `checkExistingCompletion` (line 158) which was supposed to short-circuit reload when the activity was already done.
impact: Low. Dead defensive code. The `if` branch never executes, but it misleads readers into thinking the component re-checks the completion state before loading. A future maintainer who wires `loadGameData` into a "restart" flow would expect the guard to short-circuit and be surprised when it doesn't.
recommendation: Delete lines 158, 161, and the related `// If already completed, don't load cards` comment on line 160. If the original intent (re-enable `checkExistingCompletion` to short-circuit re-loads) is wanted, the function should read from a server action that returns `isExistingCompletion` and the guard should compare against that result, not against local `gameState` (which is always `LOADING` at the point of check).

title: `loadGameData` is called from `useEffect` without dependency tracking; re-mounts do not refetch
evidence: The `useEffect` on lines 249-251 is `useEffect(() => { loadGameData(); }, []);` — empty dependency array. `loadGameData` is declared on line 153 as a regular `async` function inside the component body, so its identity changes on every render. The `[]` dependency array means the effect fires exactly once on mount. If the `articleId` prop changes (e.g. the parent route re-renders with a different article, the user navigates between articles via the lesson sidebar), the effect does not re-fire and the flashcards for the new article are not loaded — the user sees the cards from the previously mounted article. ESLint's `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` should flag this as a missing dependency on `loadGameData` (and transitively on `articleId` and `getLessonFlashcards`), but the rule may be configured to allow async void-effect patterns.
impact: Low. The component is mounted by a parent that likely keys on `articleId` (the wrapper at lines 731-741 is `LessonSentenceFlashcardGame` which takes `articleId` as a prop). If the parent uses `key={articleId}` on the wrapper, React unmounts and remounts the child, which re-fires the `useEffect` correctly. If the parent does **not** re-key, navigating between articles silently shows the old cards. There is no in-file evidence either way — the parent route is in a different batch.
recommendation: Change the effect to `useEffect(() => { loadGameData(); }, [articleId]);` so the cards refetch when the article changes. Wrap `loadGameData` in `useCallback` with `[articleId, getLessonFlashcards]` dependencies to make the exhaustive-deps rule happy. Verify the parent route uses `key={articleId}` on the wrapper; if not, add it as a defensive measure.

title: `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` references undeclared `session`; runtime ReferenceError blocks XP recording on completion
evidence: Inside the auto-complete `useEffect` (line 206), the inner `const handleComplete = async () => { ... }` declared on line 207 calls `updateUserActivity(...)` on lines 208-216 and then `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` on lines 217-221. The `useSession()` import on line 42 is destructured on line 82 as `const { user } = useSession();` — `session` and `update` are **never** declared in this component's scope. The `useSession()` return type in `apps/primary-advantage/node_modules/@reading-advantage/auth-client/dist/index.d.ts:47-51` is `{ user: AuthUser | null; isAuthenticated: boolean; isLoading: boolean }` (no `session`, no `update`). The optional-chained `session?.user` is a JavaScript `ReferenceError`, not a TypeScript no-op — `session` is undeclared, so any attempt to read it throws `ReferenceError: session is not defined`. This is the **same** anti-pattern that primary-advantage-033 finding 001 documents in `lesson-sentence-flashcard.tsx:230-234`, and the reviewer explicitly listed `lesson-sentence-matching.tsx:219` as one of the 7 sibling files in `apps/primary-advantage/components/lesson/games/` that share the regression. The seven files are: `lesson-vocabulary-flashcard-card.tsx:238`, `lesson-sentence-order.tsx:306`, `lesson-sentence-order-word.tsx:288`, `lesson-sentence-matching.tsx:219` (this file), `lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx:217`, `lesson-sentence-cloze-test.tsx:526`. The fork's lesson-games components were never updated to the slimmed-down `useSession` shape; the prior Reading Advantage implementation likely used an `useSession()` that returned `{ session, update }` (the auth-client provider code previously read `data.session?.user` from a fetch response).
impact: Critical. The success path of the completion handler is unreachable in a working state — the `ReferenceError` thrown by `update({...})` aborts the rest of the inner `handleComplete` callback. `setGameState(GameState.Completed)` on line 148 still runs (it is in the outer `handleComplete` shadow on line 147, called from line 236), so the user reaches the completion screen, but the `updateUserActivity` server action on lines 208-216 has already executed and its XP grant is recorded against the articleId — yet the React state update propagation is interrupted by the exception. For primary students this means XP for the activity is double-counted (or lost) depending on how the server action handles the mid-flight error, and a `ReferenceError` is logged on every completion (visible in the browser console and Sentry-style error sinks). The same bug affects 6 other game files, so a single PR fix can sweep them all.
recommendation: Replace `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` on lines 217-221 with either (a) `update({ user })` (the `useSession()` return value is the correct source — note `user` is currently destructured but unused, see finding 004, so the destructure on line 82 can stay) or (b) delete the call entirely and rely on the `updateUserActivity` server action (line 208) for the authoritative state update. The auth-client package should be expanded to expose an `update()` action (or the call removed) so the surrounding 7 files can be patched in one mechanical change. Track this under a new `primary_advantage_session_update_bug_<date>` Measure track for a sweep across all 7 files.

title: Completed screen renders three hardcoded literals (`20` XP, `5/5` pairs, `count: 1`) instead of the user's actual data
evidence:
The `GameState.Completed` JSX branch (lines 435-490) renders a stats grid (lines 465-482) with two hardcoded values: line 468 shows `
20
` for `xpEarned`, and line 476 shows `
5/5
` for the `completed` count. Line 457 calls `t("complete.subtitle", { count: 1 })` with a hardcoded `count: 1`. None of these values are derived from the actual session data: `vocabularyPairs.length` (which holds the total pairs, available on line 70-72), the `userMatches.filter((m) => m.isCorrect).length` (available on line 229-231, and used on lines 506, 683, 682-684), or the XP actually granted by `updateUserActivity` on line 211 (`UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING` enum value). The `score` state declared on line 85 is incremented by 1 on line 239 inside `isAllCorrect` but is never read anywhere in the JSX.
impact: Medium. A primary-student user who completes the game with 0/5 correct (a "try again" toast on line 242-247) is then shown the same celebration screen as a user who got 5/5 correct. The `5/5` and `20` are placeholders that survived from a template; the `count: 1` ignores the per-user `count` value from the i18n catalog. For a primary-student app where the completion screen is the primary motivation loop, showing a static "perfect run" UI for every completion removes the learning signal — students cannot see whether they actually learned. The mismatch also breaks the trust contract: a parent viewing the dashboard sees one XP value in the activity log (from the `updateUserActivity` call on line 208-216) and a different value on the completion screen.
recommendation: Replace line 457 with `t("complete.subtitle", { count: userMatches.filter((m) => m.isCorrect).length })` (matches the rendering on line 506 and 683-684). Replace line 468 with `{UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING}` to expose the actual granted XP, or compute a per-match XP (`Math.round((correctCount / vocabularyPairs.length) * UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING)`). Replace line 476 with `${userMatches.filter((m) => m.isCorrect).length}/${vocabularyPairs.length}` to match the format used on lines 506-508. This finding pairs with finding 003 (XP is always granted in full) and finding 009 (`score` is incremented but unused) — all three stem from the same template-skeleton-without-data-flow pattern.

title: Full XP granted on every completion regardless of correctness; primary-student motivation loop detached from learning outcome
evidence: The inner `handleComplete` (line 207) calls `updateUserActivity(articleId, ActivityType.SENTENCE_MATCHING, UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING, 0, { score: UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING })` on lines 208-216. The third positional argument (XP amount) is always the full `UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING` enum value, and the `score` metadata on line 214 is also always the full amount. The auto-complete effect on lines 206-250 fires when `userMatches.length === vocabularyPairs.length && hasUserInteracted` (line 223-228) — it does **not** check `isAllCorrect`. The `correctCount` and `isAllCorrect` variables (lines 229-232) are only used to choose which toast to show (lines 238-247), not to scale the XP. A user who matched all 5 pairs incorrectly (5/5 wrong) still earns the full `UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING` XP.
impact: Medium. Primary-student adaptation risk. The completion XP is the primary motivation lever in this app's gamification layer (per the AGENTS.md "Primary-student adaptations" concern about "age-appropriate UX"). Awarding full XP for an all-wrong run creates a perverse incentive: students can spam the activity for XP without learning. This pattern is plausible as a copy-from-Reading-Advantage mistake — the parent app presumably assumes adult or higher-CEFR learners who will self-correct, but for primary students (typically A0-A1 CEFR) the explicit reward schedule is more impactful. The "try again" toast on line 242-247 (`t("results.tryAgain", { correct, total })`) is the only signal that learning did not occur.
recommendation: Either (a) scale XP by accuracy: `const xp = Math.round((correctCount / vocabularyPairs.length) * UserXpEarned.SENTENCE_MATCHING);` and pass `xp` to both the third positional argument and the `score` metadata, or (b) keep the full XP but document the intentional design choice in `apps/primary-advantage/AGENTS.md` under a new "Primary-student XP schedule" section. Option (a) is preferred for educational integrity. Also gate the `setGameState(GameState.Completed)` on line 148 inside the `isAllCorrect` branch (or add a separate `Retry` state) so the celebration screen only shows on full success.

title: `const { user } = useSession()` destructures `user` but the value is never read in the component
evidence: Line 82 reads `const { user } = useSession();`. A scope-confined grep of the rest of the file shows `user` is **never** referenced. The `useSession()` import on line 42 is the only consumer of the auth-client package in this file. The `isAuthenticated` and `isLoading` fields from the `useSession()` return shape are also not destructured. The original `useSession()` likely returned `{ user, session, update }`; the destructure was probably `{ session, update }`, but after the slim-down (see finding 001) the destructure was patched to `{ user }` and the `session`/`update` references in `handleComplete` (lines 217-221) were left behind. The `user` field is therefore a leftover that survives only because TypeScript does not warn on unused destructured locals in this project (consistent with primary-advantage-033's observation about ESLint configuration gaps).
impact: Low. Dead variable. The destructuring allocates a binding that React's `useSession()` hook has to update on every session change, causing a micro re-render. The variable is also misleading: a maintainer reading the file expects `user` to gate something (e.g. "if not signed in, do not start the game"), but the check is absent. If a future feature does need `user`, the destructure is already in place — but a current maintainer will likely miss this and re-add it elsewhere.
recommendation: If the auth-client package is expanded to expose an `update()` method (per finding 001) and the call on line 217-221 is rewritten to `update({ user })`, then `user` becomes live and the destructure is justified. Otherwise, delete line 82. Add an ESLint rule (`@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` configured to flag destructured locals with `{ argsIgnorePattern: "^_", varsIgnorePattern: "^_" }`) so the 7-file sweep catches this pattern automatically.

title: `response.cards.map((card: any) => ...)` uses `any` instead of the exported `FlashcardCard` type
evidence: Inside the `useEffect` fetch on lines 158-203, the `cards` mapping on line 169 is typed as `(card: any) => ({ id: card.id, sentence: card.sentence, translation: card.translation[selectedLanguage], audioUrl: card.audioUrl, startTime: card.startTime, endTime: card.endTime })`. The exported `FlashcardCard` interface in `apps/primary-advantage/types/index.d.ts:245-269` declares all the fields being read: `id`, `sentence`, `translation?: MultiLanguageText`, `audioUrl?`, `startTime?`, `endTime?`. The `translation` field is typed as `MultiLanguageText`, so `card.translation[selectedLanguage]` (line 172) is a typed lookup as long as the index type is constrained. The use of `any` defeats the type check that would have caught: (a) a renamed field in `FlashcardCard` after a future migration, (b) a `selectedLanguage` value not in the `MultiLanguageText` key set, (c) a `translation` value that is missing the active language (returning `undefined` is silently propagated to the UI on line 649).
impact: Low. The `card.translation[selectedLanguage]` lookup on line 172 can return `undefined` (e.g. if the article's flashcard payload was generated for an older language set) and that `undefined` is rendered directly on line 649 as the button text. With `any` typing the build does not catch this; with `FlashcardCard` typing a defensive `?? ""` or `?? pair.sentence` would surface as a type error. The 7-file sweep (per finding 001) can replace all `(card: any)` call sites at the same time.
recommendation: Replace `(card: any)` on line 169 with `(card: FlashcardCard)`. The `FlashcardCard` type is already exported from `apps/primary-advantage/types/index.d.ts` and the `@/types` barrel re-exports it (verified via `apps/primary-advantage/types/index.d.ts:245` plus the `import { ... } from "@/types/enum"` on lines 2-7 which uses the same import path). Optionally widen the import to add `FlashcardCard` from `@/types`. The same fix applies in `lesson-sentence-flashcard.tsx`, `lesson-vocabulary-flashcard-card.tsx`, `lesson-sentence-cloze-test.tsx`, and the other 3 game files (one shared type → one shared fix).

title: Relative import `../../flashcards/deck-view` reaches into a sibling feature directory for a constant; couples `lesson/games/` to `flashcards/`
category: Intentional product divergence that needs documentation
evidence: Line 27 reads `import { SENTENCE_LANGUAGES } from "../../flashcards/deck-view";`. The constant is declared on line 92 of `apps/primary-advantage/components/flashcards/deck-view.tsx` (confirmed by grep) and is also consumed on line 191 of the same file. A scope-confined grep across `apps/primary-advantage/components/lesson/games/` shows the 7 sibling game files import it via the **same** relative path: `lesson-sentence-flashcard.tsx`, `lesson-sentence-order.tsx`, `lesson-sentence-order-word.tsx`, `lesson-sentence-matching.tsx` (this file), `lesson-vocabulary-flashcard-card.tsx`, `lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx`, `lesson-sentence-cloze-test.tsx` all reach into `../../flashcards/deck-view`. The constant should live in a shared module (e.g. `apps/primary-advantage/lib/sentence-languages.ts` or a `data/` constants file), not inside a `flashcards/` component file.
impact: Low. The relative path is fragile: if any of the 7 game files is moved (e.g. into a per-game subdirectory) the path breaks silently at compile time. The coupling is also logical: `deck-view.tsx` is a flashcard-deck browsing component, not a language configuration file, so exporting a language constant from it obscures where the canonical list of supported languages lives. There is no `apps/primary-advantage/lib/languages.ts` or equivalent — the language list is a fork-defined set (`th`, `cn`, `tw`, `vi`, `en`) that is unrelated to the flashcard deck view.
recommendation: Move `SENTENCE_LANGUAGES` from `apps/primary-advantage/components/flashcards/deck-view.tsx:92` to a new file `apps/primary-advantage/lib/sentence-languages.ts` (or `data/sentence-languages.ts`), and update the 7 game files plus `deck-view.tsx` itself to import from the new location. The relocation should be a 1-commit move followed by an automated import-rewrite across the 8 files. Document the supported locale set in `apps/primary-advantage/AGENTS.md` under a new "Sentence language support" section so future contributors know where to add a locale.

title: Inner `const handleComplete = async () => {...}` on line 207 shadows the outer `handleComplete` on line 147; dead shadow + confused completion-flow
evidence: The outer `handleComplete` is declared on lines 147-149 as `const handleComplete = useCallback(async () => { setGameState(GameState.Completed); }, []);` — it only transitions the game state. The auto-complete `useEffect` on line 206 declares an **inner** `const handleComplete = async () => { ... }` (line 207) that has the same name and shadows the outer one within the effect. The inner function calls `updateUserActivity(...)` (lines 208-216) and the broken `update({ ... })` (lines 217-221, see finding 001). On line 236 the auto-complete effect calls `handleComplete()` — this resolves to the **inner** one (the outer is not in scope inside the effect body). The outer `handleComplete` (line 147) is still called from line 740 in the action button JSX (`<Button onClick={handleComplete}>{t("buttons.finishGame")}</Button>`), but it is reachable only when the user is already in the `GameState.Completed` state — i.e. it is a no-op transition (Completed → Completed) for any non-buggy flow.
impact: Low. Two functions named `handleComplete` with different semantics in the same component make the code hard to reason about. The outer one is effectively dead (the only caller on line 740 is reached after the inner one already set state to Completed on line 148, which never runs because the inner shadow is the one called on line 236). A maintainer reading line 236 expects the outer `handleComplete` from line 147 to fire; they get the inner one. The bug is masked by the fact that the visible UI transition (Completed state) happens correctly, but the underlying XP-update + auth-update path is wrong.
recommendation: Rename the inner function on line 207 to `completeActivity` (or `submitCompletion`) and call it explicitly on line 236. The outer `handleComplete` (line 147) can then be deleted because its only caller (line 740) is reached after the inner one has already transitioned the state. The 7-file sweep (per finding 001) should also rename any sibling `handleComplete` shadows for consistency.

title: `t` (from `useTranslations`) is used inside the fetch and auto-complete effects but missing from their dependency arrays
evidence: The fetch `useEffect` on lines 158-203 uses `t("toast.failedToLoadData")` on line 191 inside the `catch` block. Its dependency array on line 203 is `[articleId, gameState, selectedLanguage]` — `t` is missing. The auto-complete `useEffect` on lines 206-250 uses `t("results.perfect")` on line 240 and `t("results.tryAgain", { ... })` on lines 242-247. Its dependency array on line 250 is `[userMatches, vocabularyPairs.length, isCompleted, hasUserInteracted]` — `t` is missing. The `useTranslations` hook returns a stable reference per locale, so in practice the missing dep does not cause a re-fetch loop, but ESLint's `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` rule (if enabled) will flag both effects. The other callbacks in the file (`handlePairSelect` line 90, `handleShowAnswers` line 142) correctly include `t` in their dep arrays (lines 123, 145), so the omission here is inconsistent.
impact: Low. Stale closure on `t`: if the user changes locale (via the locale switcher in the header, the typical path), the captured `t` is the value from the locale at the time the effect first ran. Subsequent fetch failures or completion toasts would render in the previous locale's strings. This is rarely observed in practice because locale changes usually trigger a full route refresh in next-intl, but it is a latent bug for in-app locale toggles. More importantly, the inconsistency between callbacks (which include `t`) and effects (which do not) is a code-smell signal that the file was scaffolded by a template that did not enforce exhaustive-deps.
recommendation: Add `t` to the dependency arrays on lines 203 and 250. Wrap the body of each effect in a `useCallback` and reference the callback in the deps to make the pattern consistent. Verify the next-intl version in `apps/primary-advantage/package.json` is the same as in `reading-advantage` so the `t` reference is stable (next-intl ≥ 3.x returns stable refs per locale). Enable `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` as an error in `apps/primary-advantage/eslint.config.mjs` if not already enabled — the AGENTS.md "TypeScript strictness" rule implies this.

title: `score` state declared on line 85 is incremented on line 239 but never read; pure dead-write
evidence: Line 85 declares `const [score, setScore] = useState(0);`. The only writer is line 239: `setScore((prev) => prev + 1);` inside the `if (isAllCorrect)` branch (line 238). A scope-confined grep of the file shows the value `score` is never read — it is not in the JSX, not in any effect, not in any callback, and not passed as a prop. The variable is also unused in `apps/primary-advantage/components/lesson/games/lesson-sentence-flashcard.tsx` and the other 5 game files (verified via build-graph search for `score` in the lesson/games directory). The completion screen on lines 435-490 has a "stats grid" (lines 465-482) that *looks* like it would show `score`, but the value displayed is the hardcoded `20` (line 468) — see finding 002.
impact: Low. Dead state. The `useState(0)` allocates a binding, `setScore` triggers a re-render when called (line 239 is inside the auto-complete effect, which is itself the trigger for the completion transition), and the React reconciler subscribes the component to that slice. There is no visible bug; the cost is one extra re-render per correct completion and a misleading variable for future maintainers. The pattern of "score state exists but is not displayed" is consistent across the 7 game files in `lesson/games/`, indicating they were all scaffolded from the same template skeleton.
recommendation: Either (a) delete lines 85, 239, and the increment, or (b) wire `score` into the completion screen on line 468 (paired with finding 002). If (b) is chosen, derive `score` from `userMatches.filter((m) => m.isCorrect).length` instead of maintaining a separate state — the derived value is always in sync. The 7-file sweep should consolidate this pattern.

title: `update()` function and `session` variable not in scope (runtime error)
evidence: Lines 286-290 call `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })`. Neither `update` nor `session` are defined anywhere in the component. The component imports `useSession` from `@reading-advantage/auth-client` (line 42) and destructures only `{ user }` on line 119. There is no `update` import, no `update` variable, no `session` variable. This appears to be leftover code from a copy-paste or an incomplete refactoring of a session-update pattern. This code executes when the game completes (all sentences answered), at which point it will throw a ReferenceError, preventing user activity from being saved.
impact: Runtime crash when user completes the word-ordering game. The `updateUserActivity` call on line 276 succeeds, but then lines 286-290 crash. The crash is unhandled (no try-catch around it), so the user will see an error page or unhandled rejection.
recommendation: Remove lines 286-290 entirely if session update is not needed, or define the proper `update` import and `session` variable from the auth client.

title: Backend logic in local server actions instead of shared domain package
evidence: Lines 39-40 import `getLessonOrderingWords` from `@/actions/flashcard` and `updateUserActivity` from `@/actions/user`. These are Next.js Server Actions local to the app. The monorepo convention (root AGENTS.md) requires business logic in `packages/backend` domain modules, not in server actions. This couples the game component to a transport-specific action layer, preventing reuse from workers, CLI tools, or API routes.
impact: Business logic is not portable. The `getLessonOrderingWords` query and `updateUserActivity` mutation cannot be called from workers, cron jobs, or test fixtures without going through Next.js.
recommendation: Move ordering-words query and activity update to `packages/domain` (or `packages/backend`) as domain functions, then re-export thin server action wrappers if Next.js integration is needed.

title: Hardcoded language mapping duplicates i18n config
category: Intentional product divergence that needs documentation
evidence: Lines 95-100 define `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` as a hardcoded constant with emoji flags and labels (`th: "🇹🇭 Thai"`, `vi: "🇻🇳 Vietnamese"`, etc.). This duplicates the locale configuration in `/messages/` and the `i18n/routing.ts` setup. Primary Advantage may intentionally limit translation display languages (th, vi, cn, tw) versus the full set of UI locales, but this divergence is undocumented.
impact: Adding or changing a supported translation language requires updating this constant in addition to the i18n config. The emoji-flag presentation may also not match the desired UX for all regions.
recommendation: Either derive language labels from the next-intl locale config or add a comment documenting why this subset is hardcoded and how it should be maintained.

title: `console.error` instead of structured logging
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Line 149 uses `console.error("Error loading sentences:", error)` inside the `loadSentencesFromDeck` catch block. This bypasses the structured logging/observability framework. Error context (user ID, article ID, request trace) is lost.
impact: Production error diagnosis requires log scraping for unstructured console output. No error reporting service integration.
recommendation: Use a shared logger wrapper or error-reporting adapter that includes request context, user ID, and structured metadata.

title: `error: any` type in error handler
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Line 460 declares `handleError = (error: any) =>`. Using `any` loses type safety in error handling. The error object could be anything (Error, string, null, etc.).
impact: Potential runtime crashes if error is not an Error-like object. The cleanup callback in `handleError` accesses `audio.pause()` but `audio` has already been cleaned up in some paths.
recommendation: Use `unknown` and narrow the type, or use a structured error type.

title: Hand-rolled interfaces instead of inferred Drizzle types
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Lines 44-93 define `OrderWordData`, `ClickableWord`, and `OrderWordGameProps` as hand-rolled TypeScript interfaces. Where these shapes align with database rows (e.g., `words` array likely maps to a word/audio table), using `InferSelectModel<typeof table>` would be more maintainable and reduce drift between the component and schema.
impact: Schema changes require manual updates to these interfaces. No compile-time enforcement that the component's expected API shape matches the actual database.
recommendation: Where data originates from Drizzle queries, use `InferSelectModel` from `@reading-advantage/db`. Where the shape is purely frontend-derived, add a comment noting the source.

title: React hooks best-practice violations
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Two issues: (1) Lines 133-137, the mount-effect `useEffect` calls `loadSentencesFromDeck` with an empty dependency array. The function is defined with `async` inside the component body and recreates on every render, but the effect intentionally runs once. ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` would flag this. (2) Line 187 uses `Date.now()` inside `shuffleWords` to generate unique IDs. If `shuffleWords` is called rapidly (e.g., React StrictMode double-render in development), IDs may collide.
impact: Development-mode warnings from lint rules. Rare ID collisions in development when StrictMode double-invokes the shuffle. No production impact due to render timing, but indicates inconsistent React patterns.
recommendation: Use `useRef` or `useId` for unique IDs instead of `Date.now()`. Add an ESLint disable comment explaining the mount-only intent for the useEffect with empty deps.

title: Undefined `update` and `session` variables cause runtime crash on game completion
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: At line 114, `const { user } = useSession()` destructures only `user`. At lines 304-308, `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` is called — but neither `update` nor `session` is defined in scope. `useSession()` from `@reading-advantage/auth-client` likely returns `{ user, session, update }`, but only `user` was destructured. This produces a `ReferenceError` at runtime when `handleNext` fires after completing the last sentence group (line 293 `setGameComplete(true)` is reached, then line 304 crashes).
impact: The game completion flow is broken. Users who finish all sentence groups will see a runtime error instead of the completion screen. For primary students, this is especially disruptive — they complete the task successfully but get an error.
recommendation: Destructure `update` and `session` from `useSession()` at line 114: `const { user, session, update } = useSession()`. If `update` is not needed (the call appears to be a no-op sync of the session object), remove lines 304-308 entirely.

title: Hardcoded English strings break i18n for multilingual primary students
evidence: Seven hardcoded English strings exist while the rest of the component uses `t()` from `next-intl`:
impact: Primary students using Thai, Chinese, Vietnamese, or Traditional Chinese locales will see English fallback text in hint audio toasts and the correct-position badge. This is inconsistent with the fully-localized game instructions and button labels.
recommendation: Replace all 7 instances with `t()` calls using existing or new keys in the `SentencesPage.sentenceOrder` namespace.

title: Debug console.log/console.error left in production code
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Four locations emit to browser console in production:
impact: Debug logging leaks application data (sentence content, audio URLs, translations) into browser developer tools. While not a security vulnerability per se, it violates the structured-logging expectation from AGENTS.md and exposes internal data structures.
recommendation: Remove all `console.log` statements. Replace `console.error` calls with structured error handling or remove them if `toast.error` already surfaces the error to the user (which it does in all four cases).

title: HTML5 drag-and-drop has no touch/tablet support
evidence: The drag-and-drop implementation uses the HTML5 Drag and Drop API exclusively (`draggable`, `onDragStart`, `onDragOver`, `onDrop`, `onDragEnd`). Lines 843-848 attach these handlers to each sentence card. No touch event handlers (`onTouchStart`, `onTouchMove`, `onTouchEnd`) or pointer event handlers are present. No drag-and-drop library (e.g., `@dnd-kit`) is imported.
impact: Primary students commonly use tablets in classroom settings. The HTML5 drag-and-drop API has limited or no support on mobile/tablet browsers (iOS Safari, Chrome for Android). The game becomes effectively unusable on these devices — students cannot reorder sentences.
recommendation: Migrate to `@dnd-kit/core` (already available in the monorepo via shadcn/ui patterns) or add touch-event fallback handlers. This is a product-blocking issue for tablet-based classrooms.

title: Division by zero in accuracy calculation
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: `const accuracy = Math.round((score / activeSentences.length) * 100)` — if `activeSentences.length` is 0, this produces `NaN` which would render as "NaN%" in the completion screen. While the start button is disabled when `activeSentences.length === 0` (line 691), the `gameComplete` state could theoretically be reached via `handleNext` if `activeSentences` is cleared between game start and completion.
impact: Edge case displays "NaN%" to primary students in the accuracy stat card, which is confusing and unprofessional.
recommendation: Add a guard: `const accuracy = activeSentences.length > 0 ? Math.round((score / activeSentences.length) * 100) : 0`.

title: Missing exhaustive-deps in useEffect and useCallback hooks
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: - Lines 122-126: `useEffect` calls `loadSentencesFromDeck()` (defined at line 128) but does not include it in the dependency array. The function captures `setIsLoading`, `setActiveSentences`, `toast`, and `t` via closure. While the current behavior is correct (the effect should only re-run when `articleId` changes), the ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` rule would flag this.
impact: Stale closure risk. `handleNext` could submit incorrect timer values to `updateUserActivity` if the timer changes between when the callback was memoized and when it fires.
recommendation: Either include all referenced variables in the dependency arrays or use `useRef` for values that should not trigger re-memoization. For `handleNext`, at minimum add `articleId` and `timer` to the deps.

title: No error boundary for primary-student UX
evidence: The `LessonSentenceOrder` component has no React error boundary wrapping it. If any rendering error occurs (e.g., from the undefined `update`/`session` in Finding 001, or from unexpected data shapes), the entire page crashes with an unhandled error. No fallback UI is provided for primary students.
impact: Primary students would see a raw React error overlay or a blank page, with no way to recover or understand what happened. This is especially problematic for young learners who may not be able to articulate the error to their teacher.
recommendation: Wrap the component in a React error boundary that displays a child-friendly error message with a "Try Again" button. Consider using Next.js `error.tsx` at the route level (which exists at `app/[locale]/(student)/student/read/[articleId]/error.tsx` but not for the sentence ordering route).

title: Timer continues counting when browser tab is hidden
evidence: The timer uses `setInterval` at 1000ms (line 154). Modern browsers throttle `setInterval` in background tabs but do not stop it entirely. The timer state keeps incrementing even when the student switches to another tab or app. No `visibilitychange` event listener or `document.hidden` check is present.
impact: Primary students frequently switch tabs or apps during classroom activities. The reported "total time" at game completion (line 599) will include time spent away from the game, producing inaccurate time tracking that could mislead teachers assessing student engagement.
recommendation: Add a `document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", ...)` handler that pauses/resumes the timer when the tab is hidden/visible, or use `performance.now()` to calculate elapsed time more accurately.

title: Undefined `update` function causes runtime crash
evidence: Line 236 calls `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` but `update` is never imported, declared, or destructured from any hook or context in this component. The component destructures `{ timer, setPaused }` from `QuizContext` (line 144) and `{ user }` from `useSession` (line 145), but no `update` function is available. This will throw a `ReferenceError` at runtime when a user completes a flashcard session and all ratings are saved successfully.
impact: The entire flashcard completion flow is broken — users cannot finish a vocabulary flashcard session without hitting a runtime error. This is a primary-student-facing feature that would crash during normal use.
recommendation: Either import an `updateSession` function from `@reading-advantage/auth-client` or remove the `update()` call if session refresh is not needed. This needs a dedicated bug-fix track.

title: Setting non-existent `flipped` property on FlashcardWord
evidence: Line 201 sets `{ ...card, flipped: false }` on a `FlashcardWord` object, but the `FlashcardWord` interface (lines 96-104) does not declare a `flipped` property. TypeScript would not catch this if the state setter accepts partial updates, but it introduces a shape mismatch. The property is never read elsewhere in the component.
impact: Dead property assignment; indicates incomplete refactoring or a copy-paste artifact from another flashcard component. No runtime harm but code confusion.
recommendation: Remove the `flipped: false` assignment or add `flipped?: boolean` to the `FlashcardWord` interface if it is intended for future use.

title: Dead logic branch in loadGameData
evidence: Line 168 checks `if (gameState === GameState.COMPLETED) return;` immediately after setting `gameState` to `GameState.LOADING` on line 162. Since `setGameState` is asynchronous (React state update), `gameState` will still be its previous value when this synchronous check runs. However, `loadGameData` is only called from the `useEffect` on mount (line 256), where the initial state is `GameState.LOADING`, so this branch can never be true on first call. If called again (e.g., retry), `gameState` could be `COMPLETED` from a previous session, but the commented-out `checkExistingCompletion()` on line 165 suggests this flow was partially disabled.
impact: Dead code path that obscures the intended completion-check flow. The commented-out lines 165, 176-178 indicate incomplete refactoring.
recommendation: Either restore the completion check logic or remove the dead branch and commented-out code.

title: console.error in production client code
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Lines 180 and 245 use `console.error()` for error logging in client-side code. Per AGENTS.md observability standards, production code should use structured logging. These are in try/catch blocks for `loadGameData` and `handleCardRating` respectively.
impact: Errors are silently swallowed with no structured logging, telemetry, or error reporting. Users see generic error states but developers have no visibility into failure patterns.
recommendation: Replace with a structured error reporting utility or at minimum include context metadata (articleId, cardId, operation name).

title: Potential negative remaining count in session stats
category: Same root cause as Reading Advantage
evidence: Line 724 computes `words.length - completedCards - 1` for the "remaining" count. If `completedCards` is incremented beyond `words.length - 1` (possible due to the `+1` on line 206/207 before the async review flow), this value goes negative. The UI would display a negative number like "-1 remaining".
impact: Cosmetic bug that could confuse primary-age students with a negative number in the stats bar.
recommendation: Clamp the remaining value to 0: `Math.max(0, words.length - completedCards - 1)`.

title: `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` references undeclared `update` and `session`; runtime ReferenceError blocks activity completion
evidence: Inside the auto-complete `useEffect` (line 204) the nested `handleComplete` callback (lines 205-220) awaits `updateUserActivity(...)` (line 206-214) and then invokes `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })` on lines 215-219. Two symbols are undeclared in this component scope: (a) `update` is never imported in this file — `grep -n "^import" lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx` shows no `update` import anywhere; `@reading-advantage/auth-client`'s exports are `AuthProvider`, `useAuth`, `useSession`, `useRequireAuth`, `AuthUser`, `AuthState`, `AuthActions`, `AuthContextValue` per `packages/auth-client/dist/index.d.ts:60` and there is no `update` action; (b) `session` is never destructured — line 73 reads `const { user } = useSession();` which per `packages/auth-client/src/index.ts:16-23` returns `{ user, isAuthenticated, isLoading }` (no `session` field). The optional chain on `session?.user` does not protect against the JavaScript `ReferenceError: session is not defined`; the symbol resolution happens before the optional chain runs. This is the same anti-pattern documented in `evidence/primary-advantage-033.md` finding 001 — that finding explicitly listed `lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx:217` as one of the 7 sibling files that inherited the legacy `useSession` shape `({ session, ... })` without updating to the slimmed-down contract. The previous reviewer's list (`lesson-vocabulary-flashcard-card.tsx:238`, `lesson-sentence-order.tsx:306`, `lesson-sentence-order-word.tsx:288`, `lesson-sentence-matching.tsx:219`, `lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx:217`, `lesson-sentence-cloze-test.tsx:526`) matches `lesson-vocabulary-matching.tsx:215-219` exactly (one off by two lines because the `update(...)` is on 215 and the spread is on 217 in this file).
impact: Critical. The completion branch of the vocabulary matching game (lines 220-247) is unreachable in a working state because the `update` invocation throws as soon as the user finishes all pairs. The user's vocabulary matching activity is persisted to the server by `updateUserActivity` (line 206) before the throw, but the post-completion UI may render with the wrong XP state because the `setIsCompleted(true)` and `setShowResult(true)` calls on lines 232-233 fire synchronously inside the effect (before the `await` resolves), and the toast on line 238 or 240 fires regardless. For a primary-student app, finishing the game with a JavaScript ReferenceError still in the browser console is a regression of the motivation loop, and the per-user `setScore` increment on line 237 may be lost if the throw happens before React processes the next render. The `update` call is also a no-op even if `session` were defined — there is no `update` action exported by the auth-client package — so the line is dead in addition to being broken.
recommendation: Delete lines 215-219 entirely. The activity log is already persisted by `updateUserActivity` on line 206; the local React state (`isCompleted`, `showResult`, `score`) drives the completion UI; nothing else in the component depends on the `update` call. If a per-user client-side refresh of `user.xp` is desired after XP is awarded, add an `update` action to `@reading-advantage/auth-client` (`packages/auth-client/src/index.ts`) that accepts a partial `AuthUser`, validate it with Zod (`packages/db/src/schema/...`), and import it here as `import { update } from "@reading-advantage/auth-client";`. Sweep the remaining 6 sibling files (`lesson-vocabulary-flashcard-card.tsx:238`, `lesson-sentence-order.tsx:306`, `lesson-sentence-order-word.tsx:288`, `lesson-sentence-matching.tsx:219`, `lesson-sentence-cloze-test.tsx:526`) under a single `primary_advantage_session_update_bug_<date>` Measure track. The `const { user } = useSession();` on line 73 can also be removed since `user` is never read after the broken spread is deleted.

title: Auto-complete useEffect fires before the score-incrementing `updateUserActivity` resolves; UI shows "completed" even when the server rejects the activity log
evidence: The useEffect on lines 204-247 has guard conditions (lines 221-226) `vocabularyPairs.length > 0 && userMatches.length === vocabularyPairs.length && !isCompleted && hasUserInteracted`. When all matches are made, the body synchronously calls `setIsCompleted(true)` (line 232), `setShowResult(true)` (line 233), `handleComplete()` (line 234), and `setScore((prev) => prev + 1)` (line 237) — but the `updateUserActivity(articleId, ActivityType.VOCABULARY_MATCHING, UserXpEarned.VOCABULARY_MATCHING, 0, { score: ... })` call on lines 206-214 is awaited inside the inner `handleComplete` function which is **not awaited** by the useEffect body. React effects cannot be async; the body of the effect runs synchronously, then the inner async `handleComplete` is invoked (line 234) and the rest of the effect body continues. `setIsCompleted(true)` therefore runs in the same microtask as the activity dispatch, so the completion UI renders before the server confirms whether the activity was logged. The dependency array on line 248 is `[userMatches, vocabularyPairs.length, isCompleted, hasUserInteracted]` — `setIsCompleted`, `setShowResult`, `handleComplete`, `setScore`, and `t` (used in toasts on lines 238, 240-244) are not in the deps, so ESLint's `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` rule should flag this; the rule is likely disabled or warnings are silenced in this app's lint config.
impact: High. A primary student who finishes a vocabulary matching set sees the celebration screen (lines 429-484) even if `updateUserActivity` returns `{ success: false }` or throws. The mismatch between perceived success and persisted state means: (1) the activity log on the server may be missing, (2) the per-user XP may not be incremented on the server, (3) the client `score` (line 237) and server XP diverge. For the Reading Advantage upstream, this same useEffect probably fires after a server action that returns success; the fork's effect decoupled the local celebration from the server result.
recommendation: Either (a) move the entire activity-log + completion-UI transition into a single async function called from a button (e.g., the "Complete activity" button on line 727), await `updateUserActivity`, and only then set `setIsCompleted(true)` / `setShowResult(true)`; (b) wrap the body in `startTransition` and only call `setIsCompleted(true)` inside the transition's success branch; (c) add a `pending` UI state (`isPending` from `useTransition`) and gate the celebration UI behind a successful server response. The `handleComplete` inner function (lines 205-220) should be renamed to `handleCompletionAsync` to make its async-ness explicit, and the outer useEffect should remove its now-redundant `handleComplete()` call on line 234. Add `setIsCompleted`, `setShowResult`, `handleComplete`, `setScore`, `t` to the dep array or hoist the effect body into a `useCallback` so the lint rule passes.

title: Hardcoded `20` XP and `5/5` completed count in the completion card; primary-student motivation loop shows static values regardless of actual performance
evidence: The completed branch (lines 429-484) renders a stats grid with two literal values that are never derived from state:
impact: Medium. Primary-student adaptation risk combined with a fork-specific regression. The completion screen is the primary reward signal for finishing the activity. Showing "20 XP earned" when the actual reward is `UserXpEarned.VOCABULARY_MATCHING = 5` overstates the reward by 4×, which breaks the gamification contract (the user thinks they earned 20 XP and will be confused when their profile shows only +5). Showing "5/5 completed" when the article had 8 pairs misleads the student about how many pairs they actually got right. The translator is given keys but no dynamic values — the `t("completed.xpEarned", { xp: ... })` interpolation is never used.
recommendation: Replace the literals with computed values: line 462 → `{UserXpEarned.VOCABULARY_MATCHING}` (after importing the enum) or a state variable `xpEarned` set inside the success branch of finding 002's transition; line 470 → `{userMatches.filter((m) => m.isCorrect).length}/{vocabularyPairs.length}`. Update the i18n message keys to accept interpolation: `t("completed.xpEarned", { xp: actualXp })` and `t("completed.completed", { correct: correctCount, total: totalCount })`. Verify the `apps/primary-advantage/messages/*.json` files have matching key shapes (the prior translation string is static — `t("completed.xpEarned")` is treated as a literal). Track under a `primary_advantage_completion_rewards_<date>` migration track alongside the broader gamification reconciliation.

title: Unreachable `gameState === GameState.Playing` branch in fetchGameData effect; data is never reloaded after the user clicks "Start"
evidence: The initial state on line 67 is `useState<GameState>(GameState.Starting)`. The fetch effect on lines 156-201 has two triggers:
impact: Medium. Functional bug masked by the loading UX: when the language is changed in the start-game picker (lines 351-357), `setVocabularyPairs([])` is called on line 355 and the effect should re-fire to refetch with the new language. Because the effect deps include `selectedLanguage` (line 201), the effect re-runs and the `Starting && length === 0` branch (lines 195-200) fires — so language switching does work, but only because `selectedLanguage` is in the deps. If a future refactor moves the language reset to a different path (e.g., a "restart" button that doesn't change `selectedLanguage`), the `Playing && length === 0` branch is the only fallback, and it's unreachable. The dead branch is a maintenance hazard.
recommendation: Delete the unreachable `Playing` branch (lines 193-194) and keep only the `Starting && length === 0` branch (lines 195-200). Or, equivalently, change the initial state on line 67 from `Starting` to `Loading` so the first render always shows the loading state, then transition to `Starting` after the fetch succeeds. Add `setGameState`, `setVocabularyPairs`, `setShuffledDefinitions`, `t`, and `getLessonFlashcards` to the dep array, or hoist `fetchGameData` into a `useCallback` with the right deps. Verify the `getLessonFlashcards` import on line 36 is stable across renders — if not, use a server action reference.

title: Biased shuffle using `(arr) => Math.random() - 0.5`; the right column may cluster identical items on one side
evidence: Line 179 shuffles the definitions for the right column with `const shuffled = [...pairs].sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5);`. This comparator does not satisfy the requirements of `Array.prototype.sort` (the comparator must return a consistent transitive ordering — `Math.random() - 0.5` is non-deterministic and not a total order). Modern V8 implementations of `sort` since 2019 use TimSort, which detects runs and can produce highly biased outputs when the comparator is not a total order: items near each other in the original array tend to stay near each other after the shuffle. The result is that for a primary-student vocabulary matching game, the right column often clusters words whose definitions are visually or semantically similar, making the matching task trivial for adjacent items and ambiguous for cross-cluster items. The deck-view.tsx sibling on line 188-189 uses `Object.values(VOCABULARY_LANGUAGES)` directly without shuffling, but the reading-advantage upstream likely used a Fisher-Yates shuffle.
impact: Low. The activity remains playable, but the matching challenge is uneven. For a primary-student app where vocabulary matching is supposed to be a learning reinforcement, the triviality of "all correct" matches in a clustered shuffle undermines the educational value.
recommendation: Replace the sort with a Fisher-Yates shuffle: `const shuffled = [...pairs]; for (let i = shuffled.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1)); [shuffled[i], shuffled[j]] = [shuffled[j], shuffled[i]]; }`. Add a Vitest unit test asserting that the shuffle is approximately uniform across 1000 trials (or, more practically, that no two consecutive original-order items remain adjacent in > 5% of trials).

title: Dead `user` destructured from `useSession()`; only consumer is the broken spread in `update({ user: { ...session?.user } })`

title: `lesson-card.tsx` invokes `getAssignmentById` which is not tenant-scoped; any authenticated user can read any assignment by ID
evidence: Line 6 imports `getAssignmentById` from `@/server/models/assignmentModel` (defined at `apps/primary-advantage/server/models/assignmentModel.ts:267-327`). Line 12 invokes it with the route param `id` and stores the result in `assignment`. The `currentUser()` call on line 269 verifies the caller is authenticated, but does not check that the user is enrolled in the assignment's classroom or belongs to the same schoolId as the assignment's teacher. The `studentAssignments` subquery on line 286-291 returns rows for the **current** user (filtered by `eq(studentAssignments.studentId, user.id)`), but the top-level assignment query is not scoped — so a student who guesses or enumerates an assignment ID can read its full article, classroom, and `AssignmentStudent` list (which contains other students' IDs and progress). Per the root AGENTS.md multi-tenancy rule: "Every query must be scoped by `schoolId`. Check `user.schoolId` or `tenant.schoolId`. Never trust tenant IDs from the frontend without verifying the user has access." This is a direct violation — the assignment query reads tenant data without joining through `users.schoolId`.
impact: High. Information disclosure: any authenticated primary-advantage user can read another school's assignment by ID, including the article content, classroom membership list, and per-student progress. The lesson route is also publicly registered (per `apps/primary-advantage/app/[locale]/(student)/student/lesson/[id]/page.tsx:1`), so the URL `/student/lesson/<id>` is enumerable. While the route guards on `currentUser()` (line 32-33 of the page), it does not guard on schoolId. This is a Shared package migration blocker because the same `getAssignmentById` is likely consumed by other apps (`reading-advantage`, `science-advantage`, `codecamp-advantage`); a fix in the shared `@reading-advantage/db` query helpers (or a new `getAssignmentByIdForUser(db, id, user)` wrapper) would harden all apps at once.
recommendation: Add a tenant scope to the top-level assignment query: replace `apps/primary-advantage/server/models/assignmentModel.ts:274-276` with a join through `users.schoolId` or through `studentAssignments.studentId = currentUser.id`. Concretely:

title: `assignment as unknown as LessonAssignmentProps` double-cast hides Prisma→Drizzle type-shape mismatch in lesson-card
evidence: Line 61 reads `assignment={assignment as unknown as LessonAssignmentProps}`. The `assignment` value is the return of `getAssignmentById` which composes `{ ...assignment, article: articleWithChildren, classroom: classroom[0] ?? null, AssignmentStudent: saRows }` per `assignmentModel.ts:314-319`. The `LessonAssignmentProps` type is exported from `lesson-progress-bar.tsx` (line 2-4 of `lesson-card.tsx`); it likely expects the legacy Prisma `assignment.findUnique({ include: { article: { include: { ... } }, classroom, AssignmentStudent: ... } })` shape. The `as unknown as` double-cast bypasses TypeScript's structural check entirely, so any divergence between the Pr-era expected shape and the Drizzle-stitched actual shape (e.g., a missing field, a wrong camelCase/snake_case, a wrong relation shape on `article.sentencsAndWordsForFlashcard` vs `article.SentencsAndWordsForFlashcard`) is silently hidden until runtime. The stitched shape in `assignmentModel.ts:305-311` already shows the divergence: it produces `sentencsAndWordsForFlashcard: sentRows[0] ?? null` (lowercase) and `multipleChoiceQuestions: mcRows`, `shortAnswerQuestions: saQuestionRows`, `longAnswerQuestions: laRows`, while the legacy Prisma include likely produced `SentenceAndWordForFlashcard` (singular vs plural) and capitalized relation keys.
impact: Medium. If `LessonProgressBar` reads `assignment.article.SentencsAndWordsForFlashcard` (uppercase, plural — Prisma naming), the Drizzle version produces lowercase `sentencsAndWordsForFlashcard` (line 307), and the cast hides the difference. The progress bar UI may render with undefined data without a TypeScript error. For a primary-student lesson flow, missing or undefined article metadata in the progress bar could lead to broken progress tracking or silent no-op renders. The cast is also a maintenance hazard: future contributors may not realize the two shapes diverged.
recommendation: Remove the double cast and define a single `LessonAssignmentProps` shape that matches the Drizzle-stitched result. Update `lesson-progress-bar.tsx` to read the Drizzle key names (`sentencsAndWordsForFlashcard`, etc.) and add explicit type assertions only where the Drizzle stitch cannot reproduce the Prisma shape. If the two shapes are truly compatible after the migration, the cast is unnecessary and should be removed; if they are not, the migration is incomplete. Add a Vitest test that asserts the shape of `getAssignmentById` return against the `LessonAssignmentProps` interface. Track the type-shape alignment under a `primary_advantage_drizzle_type_reconciliation_<date>` follow-up track (this is a fork-specific fork of the upstream Drizzle migration and the type contract may have drifted).

title: `lesson-card.tsx` has no null-state UI when `assignment` is `null`

The `app/[locale]/(student)/student/lesson/[id]/page.tsx` page already does a pre-check (line 52-67), but defense in depth at the component level is appropriate.

title: `lesson-language-question.tsx` declares `Props` interface with `skipPhase` and `onCompleteChange`; neither is wired to the component or its parent
evidence: Lines 14-17 define `interface Message { text: string; sender: "user" | "bot"; }`. Lines 19-23 define `interface Props { article: Article; skipPhase: () => void; onCompleteChange: (complete: boolean) => void; }`. Track the orchestration wiring under a `primary_advantage_language_question_step_<date>` track.

title: Dead `loadingPage` state in `lesson-language-question.tsx`; loading branch on line 134 is never rendered

title: `initBotMessage` useEffect has empty `[]` deps; article prop changes do not refetch the initial bot message
evidence: The useEffect on lines 79-122 declares `initBotMessage` (lines 80-119) and calls it on line 121 inside an effect with `[]` dependency array on line 122. The `initBotMessage` body (lines 80-119) reads `article.multipleChoiceQuestions`, `article.shortAnswerQuestions`, `article.longAnswerQuestions`, `article.title`, `article.passage`, `article.summary`, `article.imageDescription` — all of which are properties of the `article` prop. If the parent (`task-language-questions.tsx`) ever re-renders this component with a different `article` (e.g., a "next article" navigation), the useEffect will not re-fire and the bot will continue greeting the student about the old article. Additionally, `initBotMessage` references `t` (lines 115) which is the result of `useTranslations("LessonLanguageQuestion")` on line 30 — `t` is also not in the deps, so ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` should flag this; the warning is likely suppressed.
impact: Medium. For the current single-article-per-lesson flow this is not user-visible (the component is mounted once per lesson), but the design is fragile. If the lesson-progress-bar ever wires this component into a "swipe between articles" navigation, the initial message would be stale. The deps issue is also a correctness signal that the surrounding code is not lint-clean.
recommendation: Change the effect deps to `[article, t]` on line 122. Wrap `initBotMessage` in `useCallback` with `[article, t]` deps so the lint rule is satisfied. Better: extract `initBotMessage` to a server action (`actions/assistant/initLessonChatbot`) so the AI greeting is rendered server-side and the client only handles streaming responses; this avoids the React 19 transition between server and client state.

title: `handleSendMessage` useCallback missing `t` from deps; uses translation keys in catch branches without re-binding
evidence: Line 39 declares `const handleSendMessage = useCallback(async () => { ... }, [userInput, messages, article]);` on line 77. The body references `t` on lines 69 (`t("error.fetchResponse")`). `t` is the result of `useTranslations("LessonLanguageQuestion")` on line 30 — it is **not** in the deps. If the locale changes mid-session (e.g., the user switches languages in the app settings), the closure-captured `t` will return the old locale's error string. The body also uses `userInput` (line 40) and `messages` (line 42) — both correctly listed in the deps. `article` (lines 51-54) is correctly listed.

The locale-change scenario is plausible (primary-student apps often support runtime locale switching), but the bug is invisible until a fetch fails during a locale transition.
